page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage options. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a highly consistent, mid-tier capability profile. Multi-core processing tasks, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core tests, fall firmly within the average range. However, single-core CPU performance is a notable bottleneck, with stress-ng single-core metrics placing in the bottom 10% of tested configurations. Memory performance is mixed; while small-block cached read operations achieve average speeds, large-block uncached read and write operations are weaker, landing in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g6a.4xlarge offers a balanced resource density profile, providing dedicated x86_64 compute resources and moderate memory capacity without the premium associated with specialized hardware accelerators or high-speed local NVMe drives. This makes it a practical choice for workloads that require steady-state multi-threaded processing but do not demand extreme single-core performance or high-throughput memory access. Suitable workloads include general-purpose web serving, database operations, redis caching, and standard software compilation tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at 2.6 GHz. Built on the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 instance provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Network performance is anchored by a 5 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Benchmark data reveals average multi-core CPU and database performance, though single-core execution is relatively weak, placing in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth for large, uncached blocks also presents a performance tradeoff, scoring in the bottom 25%. Given its resource profile, the ecs.g6a.4xlarge is qualitatively cost-effective for steady-state, multi-threaded workloads. It is best suited for general-purpose applications, including static web serving, redis caching, and standard database operations that do not require high-speed local storage.
